trust_decision.summary: The mailto notifier decides that the user-supplied notify-recipient-uri (argv[1]) is a safe sendmail recipient by checking only the 'mailto:' prefix, then appends the raw remainder as a sendmail argv element. The notify-user-data Reply-To value gets the same prefix-only check before it is written into message headers.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'argument injection in mailto notifier'. The only argv construction in the file is pipe_sendmail, which appends the 'to' string unchanged.

fix_sites.entry_point: IPP Create-Printer/Job-Subscriptions (scheduler/ipp.c:5946) and Print-Job/Create-Job subscription group (scheduler/ipp.c:1894), both via cupsd_start_notifier argv[1] (scheduler/subscriptions.c:1536)
notify-user-data octets in the same IPP operations, base64-encoded into argv[2] (scheduler/subscriptions.c:1528-1537)
every event delivered on stdin to the notifier for that subscription

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: notifier/mailto.c:402 (fix.diff:264): the default Sendmail command changes to '/usr/sbin/sendmail -t', so recipients come from the headers and not from argv. This makes the Reply-To/To header values (mailto.c:289-294) part of the recipient trust boundary.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: notify-user-data only feeds the Reply-To/Sender headers, not argv, so a solver can argue it is header content unrelated to 'argument injection'. Separately, the SMTPServer transport (mailto.c:265 RCPT TO) never execs anything, so a solver can argue it is not an argument-injection route.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Ordinary RFC 5322 addresses (with '+', '.', digits, '-' inside the local part, and ?subject= query options that are stripped) must still be delivered. A site-configured 'Sendmail <path> <args...>' line in mailto.conf must keep being split into its arguments. The SMTPServer transport must keep working. lp -m / lpr -m build mailto:user@host and must keep working.

O6_input_shapes: address starting with '-' (option injection into sendmail argv)
percent-encoded characters, decoded by httpSeparateURI HTTP_URI_CODING_ALL before the character allow-list (fix.diff:125)
characters outside the dot-atom set, consecutive dots, missing or duplicate '@' (fix.diff:167-200)
the same validation applied to the notify-user-data Reply-To value (fix.diff:80-81)

O7_producer.where: notifier/mailto.c:402 (load_configuration default Sendmail string), parsed into argv by notifier/mailto.c:495-519

O8b_injection_room.sibling: add_job_subscriptions accepts notify-user-data without the mailto URI parse that create_subscriptions does at scheduler/ipp.c:6070-6083; a planted scheduler-side recipient check present in only one of the two handlers would mirror this existing asymmetry
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The two subscription handlers already differ: one checks user data and one does not, and the scheme checks differ (ipp.c:1925 vs 5973). A maintainer adding recipient validation to one handler is a realistic history.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a Cc/Bcc value taken from notify-user-data or a subscription attribute and passed to sendmail, beside the config-sourced Cc
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: mailtoCc already exists as a header slot. Letting subscribers set it per subscription is a plausible feature next to Reply-To.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the SMTP transport's RCPT TO uses the same 'to' string, a second transport to the same recipient
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already exists. A copy that validates only in pipe_sendmail would leave this transport open; it is a real second transport in the same file.

O9_family: OS argument injection (CWE-88) into sendmail argv, with adjacent mail header/recipient injection

O10_build.toolchain: autoconf ./configure + make (gcc/clang); needs libcups built in-tree
O10_build.project_tests: No mailto tests. cups/testhttp.c:112-113 and 208-209 cover httpSeparateURI on mailto URIs. The notifier binary can be driven directly with argv plus IPP event data on stdin, with a stub Sendmail command configured through CUPS_SERVERROOT/mailto.conf (mailto.c:412-415).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject a leading '-' or insert '--' before the recipient in pipe_sendmail. This leaves comma/multi-address recipient injection, the unvalidated Reply-To from notify-user-data, and the SMTP RCPT TO route open.

out_of_scope_notes: notifier/mailto.c:92-94 logs raw argv at DEBUG (the fix removed it); log-content issue, not pursued.
Subject/text from cupsNotifySubject/Text (mailto.c:155-156, 288, 299) are written into headers/body; possible header content issue, not pursued.
After the fix, a site mailto.conf 'Sendmail' line without '-t' would no longer pass any recipient; behavioural regression, not pursued.
